The Apollo 13 module pilot, Ken Mattingly, portrayed by Gary Sinise in the film, is said to have been depicted as unprepared for the flight. However, this is untrue, as Mattingly was very familiar with the module, having also worked on its development. The dialogue between ground control and the astronauts in the film was taken nearly verbatim from transcripts and recordings, with the exception of the famous line "Houston, we have a problem." The actual words spoken by Jack Swigert were "Okay, Houston, we've had a problem here."

In the film's depiction of the re-entry blackout, Tom Hanks, as Jim Lovell, says "Hello Houston... this is Odyssey... it's good to see you again." However, in the actual re-entry, the Command Module's transmission was not re-established until after the blackout had ended.

In Luke 3:23–38, Jesus' genealogy is traced back to Adam, with the Greek text of Luke using the article tou before repeating uiou (Son) except before Joseph. This genealogy descends from the Davidic line through Nathan, who is an otherwise little-known son of David, mentioned briefly in the Old Testament. In the ancestry of David, Luke agrees completely with the Old Testament, including the inclusion of Cainan between Arphaxad and Shelah, following the Septuagint text.

Augustine notes that the count of generations in the Book of Luke is 77, a number symbolizing the forgiveness of all sins. This count also agrees with the seventy generations from Enoch set forth in the Book of Enoch. Though Luke never counts the generations as Matthew does, it appears he also followed the hebdomadic principle of working in sevens. However, Irenaeus counts only 72 generations from Adam.

The reading "son of Aminadab, son of Aram", from the Old Testament is well attested. The Nestle-Aland critical edition, considered the best authority by most modern scholars, accepts the variant "son of Aminadab, son of Arni."
